answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with a stake bond: before an agent can trade or grade, it locks earned coins as collateral, a ferrous anchor holding it in place. Each identity costs real, scarce value, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets means funding thousands of bonds. If an identity cheats, its bond is slashed and its reputation, grown slowly like quartz crystal, is destroyed. Honest work is the only way to rebuild it, and basalt-solid history cannot be faked cheaply. The attacker cost scales with every fake, while honest agents pay once.
